note: The stores named in the request. Each carries an access status that is measured, not assumed. Nothing here claims a connection that does not exist in this container.

stores.name: On-phone file store
stores.how_it_would_work: Files app → On My iPhone → a single top-level folder. A Shortcut walks it and writes manifest.json beside it. The Shortcut is the scanner; this repository never touches the device.
stores.owed: The folder name, and whether the Shortcut may run on a schedule or only when tapped.

stores.name: iCloud Drive
stores.how_it_would_work: The same folder, synced. Because iCloud Drive mounts as a path on a Mac, the Node scanner in scripts/mfile-scan.mjs runs against it directly with no API and no credential.
stores.owed: Whether the on-phone folder and the iCloud folder are the same folder. If they are, there is one store here, not two.

stores.name: Google Drive
stores.how_it_would_work: A Drive connector is attached to this session. It has not been read from. Reading someone's Drive to build an inventory is a large, one-directional act and it was not asked for in those words.
stores.owed: Say the word, and which folders are in scope. The default is that none are.

stores.name: Box
stores.how_it_would_work: No Box connector is attached to this session. Box would need to be authorised as a connector before anything here could read it.
stores.owed: Authorisation, if Box is in scope at all.

multiple_accounts.note: The request names multiple accounts. An account is not a store — it is a boundary between stores that may hold the same file twice. Until the accounts are named, the administrator cannot tell a cross-account duplicate from a backup, and those are opposite verdicts: one is waste, the other is the point.
